` [Highlight start] Alcohol does not directly react with amoxicillin or stop it from working [Highlight end] ` , though doctors generally recommend avoiding or limiting alcohol while recovering from an infection.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF10q-UeoPkGlvrL2KcM_M71xsxh1DAfZV2om9jtyyKzLxwoMFyyWLK3brQlLBNMEKTks23_j-3Y38Jacx6BruREWnIcPqF0bZTyYycwNB-mtlIk_Kt4jGLw6SBKpldbWe3DYA1cVTs8BL5AkEfmio9Df0eS4CH1piNmPCpumZHmty7aKGHoVWjWGM4gokGIg)

### Why Caution Is Still Recommended

- **Worsened side effects:** Both amoxicillin and alcohol can cause stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or dizziness. Combining them can make these symptoms worse.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqwEBxCJF16poOIOul2bSCviQwEplDGv_LOhw7hIffru7ano6Heprx2-MUC5PTESzsBXmTeUiMVUPLIstgwxzXhRPNuIXko6dI0z28PUsa_i1eLohRP6t9dNPgLuRmA8KZFgFok5lXooOI4qcJGvaE7oCLIoBhawx90gl0x-eoXr9Ol85l61aobbfLaqlnWkqRg0FhHDnUqHLFpXFxeu5rUlGT0CVSAQSqxs1xj8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1zMWUeswezP31xDG4489AO92cwGHkiHczm3NrxyxSH6BAxeJAnF0FHcp6t-CDaPkIuXbXxxZ_QsfDYW9l6ZUwb9EIBZQ9In2SVYam-jK0xnICc0I3pfeGk6XMdGgJjs4-Ds8CGU8v563xWgm72yv-koEMEp1_USdPLgafhznWx1sRuQCrMdrmzo3cv0)
- **Slower recovery:** Alcohol causes dehydration, disrupts sleep, and lowers energy, which can slow your body's healing process. Heavy drinking can also weaken immune defenses and make it easier to miss doses.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjgEBxCJF1_Yomo4kfKq21Jnv6yvGkRfpOvkNuZGD4TIh-Xv1SS7csml0OHNOj_ky83g51BDPMIE6DRcL70wXHR3PhYUv89Zaf9H6CuWH4mIToiG0Y_B_G1d7mBlmgu7ADxzQ8Gg9abg8LijMY91lDZZEn8sBUjFOMPXuCfKOl3qAev3R9FWyFmFPo2Y7X2RQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF10q-UeoPkGlvrL2KcM_M71xsxh1DAfZV2om9jtyyKzLxwoMFyyWLK3brQlLBNMEKTks23_j-3Y38Jacx6BruREWnIcPqF0bZTyYycwNB-mtlIk_Kt4jGLw6SBKpldbWe3DYA1cVTs8BL5AkEfmio9Df0eS4CH1piNmPCpumZHmty7aKGHoVWjWGM4gokGIg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqwEBxCJF16poOIOul2bSCviQwEplDGv_LOhw7hIffru7ano6Heprx2-MUC5PTESzsBXmTeUiMVUPLIstgwxzXhRPNuIXko6dI0z28PUsa_i1eLohRP6t9dNPgLuRmA8KZFgFok5lXooOI4qcJGvaE7oCLIoBhawx90gl0x-eoXr9Ol85l61aobbfLaqlnWkqRg0FhHDnUqHLFpXFxeu5rUlGT0CVSAQSqxs1xj8)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1zMWUeswezP31xDG4489AO92cwGHkiHczm3NrxyxSH6BAxeJAnF0FHcp6t-CDaPkIuXbXxxZ_QsfDYW9l6ZUwb9EIBZQ9In2SVYam-jK0xnICc0I3pfeGk6XMdGgJjs4-Ds8CGU8v563xWgm72yv-koEMEp1_USdPLgafhznWx1sRuQCrMdrmzo3cv0)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXXxVmK-NuqCUhJVH0KGbbpWq6z6hSpIOtV7abwBt192YPoWvKO3p06pTuKPuO56_lHk2faxtzLNJd4QVAB3mxwN7LOrsVhe9fWzTXFIvQXXjxkG-gzNR8b-Q12it6rfDci8YXnU18UXzTLLb_Nq2AUU_CPt1VOgoIIVP8)

items.title: Why Caution Is Still Recommended
items.text: Worsened side effects: Both amoxicillin and alcohol can cause stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or dizziness. Combining them can make these symptoms worse. Slower recovery: Alcohol causes dehydration, disrupts sleep, and lowers energy, which can slow your body's healing process. Heavy drinking can also weaken immune defenses and make it easier to miss doses. Absorption timing: While alcohol doesn't cancel out amoxicillin's overall effect, it can slightly slow how quickly the drug is absorbed in the stomach.

items.title: Practical Tips
items.text: Stick to your schedule: If you have a light drink, you do not need to skip doses or restart your prescription. Finish the full course as directed. Consider waiting: Many people prefer to skip alcohol until they finish their course and feel completely well, or wait 1 to 2 days after the last dose if they had side effects. Check other medications: Avoid alcohol if you are taking other drugs that interact with it (such as certain pain relievers or other antibiotics like metronidazole or Bactrim). You can also use the Drugs.com drug interactions checker to verify other medications you take.
